newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end sharply up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end sharply up on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices staged a sharp comeback Wednesday after concerns about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin fueled a heavy bout of short covering and pulled the oil complex out of negative territory.
"Everybody and their brother had gone short this thing which lead to a whole lot of short covering on wide speculation," said Mike DeLuca, trader with Prudential Securities.
February crude settled up 84 cents at $25.95 a barrel. Feb heating oil ended up 2.00 cents a gallon at 71.42 cents, and Feb gasoline finished up 1.81 cents a gallon at 68.85 cents.

On Wednesday, Yeltsin was ordered by his doctors to stay in hospital all week due to a serious bout of pneumonia. Yeltsin's Communist rivals in Russian parliament called for a vote for his ouster on the grounds of ill health.
The news sent traders with short positions scrambling to buy as the market viewed the political instability as threatening Russia's oil production, which is among the largest the world.
"We started to buy around $25.00 during the Yeltsin talk, but it was overblown," said one trader with a large fund in New York regarding the market's reaction.

The chief Kremlin doctor, Sergei Mironov, told a news conference Wednesday that Yeltsin's condition had "stabilized considerably" but that the 65-year-old president, who had initially insisted on only three days in hospital, had been persuaded he needed more time there.

Although Wednesday's rally snapped two consecutive days of declines, dealers said prices were still vulnerable to the downside after the American Petroleum Institute (API) Tuesday showed increasing oil supplies.
The API said gasoline stocks grew 415,000 barrels compared with expectations of a build of more than two million barrels for the week ended January 10.
But, the Department of Energy's (DOE) Energy Information Administration (EIA) said Wednesday that in its own inventory data, gasoline stocks rose 1.8 million barrels
Crude stocks also grew, rising a large 4.7 million barrels, the API said.

Distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, fell 1.3 million barrels, just about matching expectations. Dealers noted the API report showed that the distillate stock shortfall with a year ago has narrowed to a mere 350,000 barrels from almost 20 million last August.
